title: Docs + enablement: runbooks and migration notes for KV/prefix cache telemetry v2
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Owners: Platform + SRE (docs lead: Elliot Price; customer-facing tech writing: Wei Chen)

Background
We’re shipping KV/prefix cache telemetry v2 (new metric names, tag rules, sampling/cardinality budgets, and new dashboard/alert semantics). To prevent breakage and noisy oncall, we need (1) updated internal runbooks and (2) migration notes for teams consuming cache metrics (SRE, Optimize, Console dashboards, Customer Support, Solutions).

Scope
1) Internal enablement docs (Confluence)
- Migration notes for v2 cache telemetry (what changed, why, how to update queries/alerts/dashboards).
- Deprecation plan and timelines for v1 metric names (including an explicit “overlap period”).
- Compatibility notes by deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), including attribution gaps/constraints.

2) Runbooks (Confluence)
- Data quality runbook updates (missing metrics, sampling misconfig, tag explosion symptoms, cardinality guardrail drops).
- SRE oncall runbook updates for the new cache hit-rate regression alerts (triage steps + links to dashboards).
- Enablement how-to: feature flags per region/tier + staged rollout checklist + rollback triggers.

3) Supporting artifacts
- Metric/tag mapping table (old → v2) with “allowed / hashed / aggregated” tag policy.
- Quick “FAQ” section for Support/Solutions: how to interpret hit-rate vs saved_prefill_ms, and common causes of mismatches (partial-prefill, streaming retries, routing fragmentation).
- “Known issues” callouts and mitigations that we can point customers to during rollout.

Out of scope
- New UI polish for Console (beyond whatever is already in flight).
- Rewriting the entire observability standards section; we will link to the v2 spec/ADR.

Deliverables / Links
- Confluence (canonical spec + ADR)
  - kv-cache-telemetry-v2-metric-spec (architecture-and-standards)
  - ADR-027 kv cache metric cardinality budget
- Confluence (runbooks/how-tos)
  - Cache telemetry data quality runbook (eng-platform/runbooks)
  - Enabling cache telemetry feature flags (eng-platform/how-tos)
  - Cache hit-rate regression alerting (eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets)
  - Cache hit-rate misclassification known issues (eng-serving-runtime/known-issues)
- Working docs (Drive)
  - Cache metric tag mapping sheet (old → v2)
  - Cache telemetry rollout plan working doc
- Code/docs PR(s)
  - redwood-docs PR-611 (customer-facing + internal doc updates)
  - observability-pack PR-921 (dashboard JSON + alert templates reference links)

Acceptance criteria
- Migration notes page includes:
  - v1 → v2 metric name mapping (and which v1 metrics are removed vs aliased)
  - tag changes + cardinality constraints (what must be aggregated; what must never be used as a dimension)
  - recommended dashboard queries (hit-rate, hit-bytes, saved_prefill_ms, cacheable_prompt_ratio)
  - explanation of hit-rate vs savings (saved_prefill_ms) and how partial-prefill is classified
  - deprecation/overlap timeline and an explicit “what will break” section
- Runbooks updated and reviewed:
  - Data quality runbook reviewed by Caleb Johnson (ingestion) and Nadia Rahman (pipeline)
  - Alerting runbook reviewed by Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes (oncall)
  - Enablement/feature-flag doc reviewed by Connor O’Brien (rollout coordinator)
- Rollout comms ready:
  - Slack announcement draft (eng-platform + eng-sre) including links to migration notes + runbooks
  - Support-ready snippet (short) for “why did my cache hit-rate change?”

Notes / Risks
- Avoid duplicating the v2 spec in multiple places; migration notes should link to the spec + ADR and focus on “what to do.”
- Private deployments: ensure language clearly states when route/model/version attribution may be missing or reduced depending on gateway/control-plane version.
- Be explicit about sampling: users must not treat low-volume per-route segments as authoritative when sampling is enabled.

Requested reviewers
- SRE: Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes
- Platform/Telemetry: Logan Wright, Caleb Johnson, Nadia Rahman
- Rollout: Connor O’Brien
- Product (Optimize): Aditya Rao (sanity check recommendation input fields mention)

Definition of done
- Confluence pages updated (or new pages published) and linked from the ENG-4812 umbrella.
- redwood-docs PR merged (or at minimum ready-to-merge with sign-offs).
- Support/Solutions snippet posted in #customer-support-internal and linked from SUP-3921.
